title: ANSMET: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with Near-Memory Processing and Hybrid Early Termination
problem: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) over large high-dimensional vector databases is both highly memory-bound and computationally wasteful: a large fraction of fetched vectors and their distance computations are ultimately discarded because many candidate vectors are far from the query. This dual inefficiency — excess memory traffic and low data utilization — limits throughput and energy efficiency on general-purpose computing platforms.
motivation: Vector databases are growing rapidly for LLM retrieval-augmented generation and recommendation systems; ANNS at scale requires processing billions of high-dimensional vectors with tight latency budgets, making the memory bandwidth bottleneck and wasted computation a critical design problem.
method: ANSMET co-designs a near-data processing (NDP) architecture at the memory rank level with a hybrid partial-dimension/bit early termination strategy. Distance calculation and comparison for ANNS are offloaded to near-data units within memory ranks, eliminating main memory bandwidth consumption for rejected vectors. As a vector is streamed from memory, ANSMET conservatively estimates a lower-bound distance using partial dimensions and/or partial bits of each element; if this lower bound already exceeds a threshold, the fetch and computation are terminated early. Data layout within a single memory access and across multiple memory ranks is co-optimized to match the early termination granularity, and a lightweight host-NDP coordination protocol manages index traversal and result sorting.
key_novelty: The hybrid partial-dimension/bit early termination strategy conservatively estimates distance lower bounds during streaming to skip unnecessary data fetches, combined with rank-level near-data processing to eliminate host memory bandwidth consumption for rejected ANNS candidates.
contributions: A rank-level near-data processing architecture for ANNS distance calculation and comparison that eliminates off-chip data movement for rejected vectors.
A hybrid early termination strategy combining partial-dimension and partial-bit distance lower-bound estimation during incremental vector fetching.
Co-optimized data layout within and across memory ranks to align with early termination granularity and maximize rank-level parallelism.
5.26x average speedup from NDP alone, plus an additional 1.52x from hybrid early termination on top.

metrics.speedup: 5.26x average from NDP; additional 1.52x from hybrid early termination (total ~8x)

baselines: general-purpose computing platform (CPU/GPU baseline for ANNS, unspecified)
limitations: Not discussed; the impact of early termination recall degradation on end-to-end retrieval quality is not quantified.
primary_theme: Near-memory processing with hybrid early termination for ANNS
